matters.text: The City of Green Bay operates 25 sanitary sewer and stormwater lift stations. These stations are controlled by obsolete electronic hardware that is increasingly expensive to maintain and difficult to service. In addition, the software that controls the lift stations is outdated and provides limited functionality for system monitoring, data logging, and operational review. To address these challenges, the City is upgrading the electronic hardware to modern, readily available, and easily serviceable units. The project also includes implementation of updated software to provide improved reliability, increased visibility for on-call staff, and expanded data logging and reporting.

Onalaska’s water and sanitary system consists of four wells, three booster stations,
five reservoirs, one control valve, ten lift stations, one meter pit, and one storm lift
station. The water distribution system consists of multiple pressure zones. The system

to communicate with the main utility office via unlicensed spread spectrum radios.

reservoirs to control each well and booster pump as well as switch between summer and
winter setpoints for each of the reservoirs. The purpose of the summer and winter
setpoints is to maintain a wider range of levels and create turnover in the storage facilities
during the winter months to prevent ice from forming. Because of the number of
reservoirs in the system, water age and chlorine residual in the reservoirs were also
concerning. Therefore, temperature probes were added to each reservoir to enable
operators to monitor the temperature in each reservoir and adjust pumping sequences to
promote more frequent turnover in any given reservoir.

matters.text:
Reason for Request: To permit the development of a military veteran preferred small home cottage court on a 3.46-acre property, yet to be divided. 
 Subject Parcel Zoning and Land Use: Subject land area is zoned Public Institutional (PI) District and is undeveloped green space. The property was formerly the location of the Brown County Mental Health Center.
 Surrounding Zoning and Land Uses: 
 North: Public Institutional (PI) | Veteran Preferred Multi-Family Residential 
 South: Public Institutional (PI) | Green Space
 East: Public Institutional (PI) | Green Space
 West: Varied Density Residential (R3) | Multi-Family and Assisted Living Residential
 Comprehensive Plan: The 2022 Smart Growth Plan designates this area for other Public or Semi-Public Uses. Public or Semi-Public Uses are defined as “public buildings and public facilities, buildings for private organizations that are supported heavily by public funds and donations, hospitals and closely associated medical clinics (even though they may be privately owned), places of worship and cemeteries”. The proposed development is a mix of residential and social service activity and falls within the category of private organization heavily funded by public resources. The proposed use is not in conflict nor inconsistent with the recommendation of the Comprehensive Plan.
Even though the proposed use is not inconsistent with the future land use recommendation, the underlying zoning of the property will remain Public Institutional (PI) District and the city will utilize the Planned Unit Development Overlay (PUD) District to facilitate this request. Per code, the use of a PUD is a means to enable the development of land in an integrated and innovative fashion, to allow for flexibility in site design, and to encourage development that is sensitive to environmental, cultural, and economic considerations. It also provides the City Council with the ability to establish any reasonable conditions of approval determined to be necessary to mitigate potential adverse impacts. By using the PUD and not changing the underlying zoning, the City’s future land use designation will remain PI should the development not occur. This is meaningful as the property is currently owned by Brown County and would be retained by the County should the project not come to fruition. If the project is constructed and in operation, staff will review the future land-use for the area and likely bring forward recommended changes to the future land use plan to reflect the character of the proposed low-medium density residential development. 
 Analysis: The request before the Plan Commission is for approval of a PUD for the development of a 21 small home cottage court to be developed in three phases. The units are proposed to be veteran preferred and complemented with a variety of social and supportive services for tenants/residents. This project will incorporate two primary elements:
1. New housing opportunities in the form of a single-family home cottage court including the development of 21 “small” single-family detached structures: 17 - 400 square foot homes
 4 - 600 square foot homes
 Storage garage
 Community center
 Pavilion
 Garden areas
 Two surface parking lots 
 2. Social and Support Services will be limited to residents of the development and be administered by qualified/licensed professionals with assistance of trained volunteers. Social and supportive services activities will include: Active case management. Case management will be required for individuals enrolled in the rapid rehousing program and individuals receiving HUD VASH vouchers
 Employment and career services
 Group and individual mental health therapy
 Physical wellness activities such as yoga, tai chi, massage, and chiropractic services
 Mental health counseling services 
 Financial literacy programs
 The overall development area is approximately 3.46 acres of land currently part of a larger 33-acre parcel owned by Brown County but designated to be divided off and deeded to the petitioner upon zoning approval. It is located on the City’s east side at 2890 St. Anthony Drive, approximately 1/3 of a mile south of the Curry Lane/St. Anthony Dr. intersection and approximately 1/10 of a mile north of Mt. Mary Drive intersection. A veterans preferred apartment building is adjacent to the north, Brown County property including an unmarked cemetery is located to the south on their 33-acre property, and an additional 225-acres of Brown County owned lands are to the north, northeast and east. A majority of the land is undeveloped but lands with frontage on St. Anthony Dr. and Curry Lane include Brown County Shelter Care, Curative Connections and ProSolutions, Brown County Sheriff’s Dept., Brown County Jail and Juvenile Detention Center, and Brown County Nursing Home. Lands across St. Anthony Drive are developed with several medium density apartment complexes, a nursing home/post-hospital rehab facility, a residential senior living and memory care facility, and Freedom House Ministries Shelter.
The proposed 21 small home cottage court is projected to be completed in three phases. Phase 1 is proposed to include a 25-foot-wide private roadway from St. Anthony Dr., pedestrian sidewalks, 5-400 square foot single story homes, 2-600 square foot single story, and a 14-stall surface parking facility.
 Phase 2 shall consist of 7-400 square foot single-story homes, a 3,150 square foot single-story community center, a 1,200 square foot single-story garage, a 14-stall surface parking facility, a 250 square foot single-story pavilion, and a communal garden area.
 Phase 3 shall consist of 5-400 square foot single story homes, 2-600 square foot single story homes, and a communal garden area.
The homes are proposed to have a minimum lease term of 30 days and occupancy will be limited to one tenant/occupant in each of the 400 square foot homes and two tenants/occupants in each of the 600 square foot homes. All potential residents will be screened prior to leasing including a vigorous intake procedure as detailed in the submitted operating procedures as well as the use of CCAP, Green Bay Municipal Court records, sex offender registry, and US Dept. of Justice website. 
All homes and other structures are proposed to be single story. The homes and other structures will be set back greater than 400 feet from St Anthony Dr right-of-way, except for a community identity sign, and setback from the side yards to the north and the south no less than 10 feet from the future property line. As proposed, all home building designs will include an open gable roof, covered front porch, primary front façade window and windows on all sides of the homes. The buildings shall be clad in horizontal vinyl siding. While the structures are modest in size, staff feels they can attain the same level of architectural character as other homes within the city and staff recommends their exterior characteristics be enhanced to include shake siding in the gable ends of both the covered porch and home itself, an additional window be added on both side façades of the structure, be a minimum of 3 distinct and different siding colors for homes so no more than 7 of the 21 homes will have the same siding color. All window and door openings are also recommended to include trim in a contrasting color to the siding. Front porches are recommended to include railing that matches the color of the home’s trim. The community center, garage and pavilion are not currently designed but must meet the building standards located within the Zoning Code.
Access to the development will consist of a single private roadway off St. Anthony Drive. It is proposed to be 25 feet wide accessing the entirety of the site and shall be terminated in a cul-de-sac or other “turn-around” acceptable to Green Bay Metro Fire Department and the Department of Public Works. Pedestrian access shall be provided in the form of a paved, 5-foot wide sidewalk/trail providing pedestrian access from St. Anthony Drive to all structures within the development area. Additionally, staff recommends that painted crosswalks and pedestrian crossing signs be included across the private roadway at the locations of the parking facilities. Motor vehicle parking shall consist of 28 parking stalls within two, 14-stall surface parking facilities and one utility garage.
Lighting throughout the PUD area will need to meet the standards as set forth within zoning code and will also include “dusk to dawn” security lighting installed throughout the PUD area and more specifically between the homes and at the community center. Approximately 12 security cameras will be installed throughout the PUD area and Green Bay Police will be provided access to surveillance upon request according to the submitted operations plan. Two management/security staff will be on-site weekdays from 8 a.m. – 5 p.m. At nights and weekends, there will be one resident designated as on-site management/security person for every 7 homes developed and occupied.
Landscaping throughout the PUD area shall meet the standards as set forth within the Green Bay Municipal Code as if the overall project area was a multiple family use adjacent to residentially zoned property. Specific attention shall be given to screening parking lots from adjacent property.
The petitioner began looking for a site to create a veteran preferred cottage court, which is based off others around the country, a few years ago. They indicated that in 2021 the Greater Green Bay Community Housing Initiative Task Force published the Blueprint Study that identified 3,715 residents who needed affordable housing and veterans made up 13% of that population. Veterans 1st of NEW began discussions with property owners and went before the Brown County Board of Supervisors on December 20, 2023, where they were granted approximately 3.46 acres of property from the County’s approximately 260 acres in the area by a 24-0 vote. Additionally, staff recommends that painted crosswalks and pedestrian crossing signs be included across the private roadway at the locations of the parking facilities. Motor vehicle parking shall consist of 28 parking stalls within two, 14-stall surface parking facilities and one utility garage.
Lighting throughout the PUD area will need to meet the standards as set forth within zoning code and will also include “dusk to dawn” security lighting installed throughout the PUD area and more specifically between the homes and at the community center. Approximately 12 security cameras will be installed throughout the PUD area and Green Bay Police will be provided access to surveillance upon request according to the submitted operations plan. Two management/security staff will be on-site weekdays from 8 a.m. – 5 p.m. At nights and weekends, there will be one resident designated as on-site management/security person for every 7 homes developed and occupied.
Landscaping throughout the PUD area shall meet the standards as set forth within the Green Bay Municipal Code as if the overall project area was a multiple family use adjacent to residentially zoned property. Specific attention shall be given to screening parking lots from adjacent property.
The petitioner began looking for a site to create a veteran preferred cottage court, which is based off others around the country, a few years ago. They indicated that in 2021 the Greater Green Bay Community Housing Initiative Task Force published the Blueprint Study that identified 3,715 residents who needed affordable housing and veterans made up 13% of that population.
